drivingQuestion: Are relatives of the guarantor valid witnesses on the promissory note?
outcomeNote: Rav Pappa's initial view is rejected

segments.he: אִילְעָא וְטוֹבִיָּה, קָרִיבֵיהּ דְּעָרְבָא הֲוֹה. סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא לְמֵימַר: גַּבֵּי לֹוֶה וּמַלְוֶה רַחִיקִי נִינְהוּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא: אִי לֵית לֵיהּ לְלֹוֶה, לָאו בָּתַר עָרְבָא אָזֵיל מַלְוֶה?
segments.en: Apropos disqualified witnesses, the Gemara relates: Two people called «Ile’a and Tuviyya,» who signed as witnesses on a promissory note, «were relatives of the guarantor» of the loan. «Rav Pappa thought to say» that since «vis-à-vis the borrower and lender» these witnesses «are distant» and are not related, their testimony on the document is valid. «Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rav Pappa: If the borrower does not have» the means to repay the loan, «doesn’t» the «lender pursue the guarantor» to claim his debt? Therefore, the guarantor is party to the loan, and his relatives are not eligible to serve as witnesses on the promissory note.
